units.translation: 41-43a. But he to the bronze-forge: of the islands of Aeolus there is the one called Hiera, in which they say Hephaestus forges bronze. He has called it 'wandering' following those who relate the wanderings of Odysseus around Italy and Sicily; or because in ancient times all the islands wandered and had no fixed bases. But Callimachus says that not Hiera is dedicated to Hephaestus, but Lipara (Hymn III 47) 'on the island of Lipara'. These are the seven islands of Aeolus: Strongyle, Euonymus, Hiera, Lipara, Didyme, Ericodes, Phoenicodes. <...> around Sicily.

b. Callias relates in the tenth book of his work On Agathocles (fr. 4 M. II 383), saying that there is a high hill there, on which are two craters, one of which has a circumference of three stades, from which much light is emitted, so that it illuminates the sea far and wide. Then from the chasm are thrown up fiery stones of immense size. And such a loud noise occurs at the time when Hephaestus happens to be working, that the sound is heard for five hundred stades. The masses hurled up by the blast are always violet-colored because of the burning, and they have the appearance and power of things that have been burnt. At night, then, all the things that happen around the work of the god are clearly revealed, but by day from the summit, whence the flame rises, a kind of cloud is seen hanging over it. And by saying 'he forged intricate works with the blast of fire' he indicates the so-called upblowing of fire from the chasm mentioned by Callias.
